passage:
"Mummy, look!" Ritu held up her paper. "A bus!"
"Oh, I love it," said Mummy. "And look at all these windows. You gave every person a different hat."
"That is the driver. He has a stripey one."
"How did you get the wheels so round?"
"I traced the bowl."
Zubin, her little brother, hopped up. "Me too?"
"You can draw yours next," said Mummy.
Ritu grinned, glowing. "I will stick it on the fridge myself."

qa.q: How did Ritu make the wheels so round?
How does Ritu feel when Mummy looks at the drawing?
qa.a: She feels a warm glow of pride, and it grows as Mummy notices details, so she wants to display it herself. 🙂

qa.q: What did Mummy do that a wise parent would do?
qa.a: She noticed specific details like the windows and hats and asked a question about the wheels, rather than only saying good.

qa.q: What might Zubin be feeling as he hops up?
qa.a: He seems keen to join in and share the attention, and Mummy's reply shows his turn is coming.

grounding: A parent looks at the child's drawing and shows love for it by noticing details, and the child feels a warm glow.
